title: Laughing is listed at 6 months, after a chuckle that is not a full laugh
summary: The CDC lists a chuckle that is not yet a full laugh at 4 months, and laughing at 6 months.
body: On the 4-month social and emotional list, the CDC says most babies chuckle, and it adds that this is not yet a full laugh, when you try to make the baby laugh. On the 6-month social and emotional list, the page simply says laughs. Both lines sit under what most babies do by that age, not under the language heading. Laughing is not the same item as squealing, which the 6-month page files with language. The ages are the United States CDC marks.
